For 2≤j≤p the only allowed resonance is s=j, which is in range precisely when j≤(p+1)/2. Subtracting a multiple of f at that entry leaves only the free tail s>p+2−j, of dimension j−1. At j=1 the last diagonal coefficient is p=0, and f and x^(p+1) account for both degrees of freedom; order p+1 is central. The x^(p+1) quotient truncates the same triangular system one step earlier and removes only the j=1 top resonance from that range; its cutoff for the s=j resonance stays the same because p is odd. Counting zero and each order with its q^dim centralizer gives both polynomials and the fixed-p limiting ratio. The classes of e_2 and e_p commute downstairs but all lifts have the same bracket (p−2)e_(p+1)≠0, including p=3. The quantitative comparison distinguishes the actual central extension from a split stabilization: their leading commuting counts differ by a factor tending to 2/(p+1), and the deficient lift is explained by the surviving degree-p+1 commutator. The exact order strata make the result reusable for finite fields.
